title: Review of Health Knowledge Graphs for Clinical Decision Support: Construction, LLM-Grounded Reasoning, and Applications
content: Health Knowledge Graphs (Health-KGs) structure heterogeneous medical information from Electronic Health Records (EHRs), the biomedical literature, and clinical guidelines into machine-reasonable form, and have become a foundation for clinical decision support. This work reviews the construction and application of Health-KGs following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, organizing the literature along three axes representation, extraction, and integration and situating it against prior biomedical-KG reviews. We examine knowledge-representation learning and graph-embedding models, named-entity recognition, disambiguation, and linking, and cross-source integration, together with the principal EHR datasets and clinical language models that underpin them. A distinguishing focus is the shift toward large language models (LLMs): we synthesize LLM-driven entity and relation extraction, retrieval and graph-augmented clinical reasoning, and the factuality and hallucination constraints that govern their safe use an axis not addressed by prior EHR-focused reviews. We further reviewed applications spanning drug development and clinical trials, diagnosis and prediction, treatment recommendation, question answering, and health-policy compliance. Finally, we identify the central open challenges: the absence of a standardized, openly governed Health-KG benchmark; heterogeneous and temporally evolving clinical data; multimodal fusion; and privacy-preserving, reproducible construction. This review is intended as a roadmap for data scientists, medical-informatics and AI researchers, and healthcare practitioners.
